item.title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval to expand transfer of convicted offenders agreements
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina President Bola Tinubu has transmitted a bill seeking to amend the Transfer of Convicted Offenders (Enactment and Enforcement) Act to the House of Representatives for consideration, with a view to extending its application to countries outside the Commonwealth. In a letter dated October 20, 2026, addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, Tinubu urged lawmakers to consider the proposed legislation expeditiously. The bill, titled Transfer of Convicted Offenders (Enactment and Enforcement) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, seeks to amend the existing law, Cap. T16, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. According to the President, the proposed amendment is designed to give effect to schemes or agreements between the Federal Government of Nigeria and other countries for the transfer of convicted offenders. The amendment would also empower the President, through an order published in the Federal Gazette, to extend the application of the Act to any country with which Nigeria has entered into such an agreement. Tinubu said the proposed change would enable Nigeria to implement agreements concluded with countries outside the Commonwealth, potentially broadening the scope of international cooperation on the transfer of convicted offenders. Transmitting the bill pursuant to Section 58(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the President formally requested the consideration of the House of Representatives. “While it is my hope that the House of Representatives will consider this submission expeditiously, please accept, Rt. Hon. Speaker, the assurances of my highest consideration,” Tinubu stated in the letter. The bill is now before the House for consideration. The presidential communication did not specify the countries that could be covered by future agreements or provide details of the proposed implementation arrangements. item.title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval for ₦269.4bn promissory notes to settle FG debts
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to approve the establishment and expansion of the Federal Government’s Promissory Note Programme to settle outstanding verified liabilities totalling ₦269.44bn. This was contained in a letter by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume which was read on the floor of the House during plenary in Abuja. The request is aimed at addressing outstanding contractual, project-related and other financial obligations owed to various categories of creditors. In a letter dated August 18, 2026, and received by the Office of the Speaker on October 21, Akume said the liabilities amounted to ₦269,446,402,822.56, following a comprehensive review by relevant ministries, departments and agencies. He said Tinubu had approved the proposal to establish and expand the programme as a mechanism for settling the verified obligations. According to the letter, the programme is designed to provide “a structured, transparent and fiscally responsible framework” for settling the outstanding debts, while ensuring that only verified and validated claims are admitted. The President is seeking legislative approval for the issuance of promissory notes worth ₦269.44bn, or such other amount as may be approved by the National Assembly, to settle the liabilities contained in the accompanying schedule. The request also seeks approval for the inclusion of the identified categories of liabilities and beneficiaries in the programme, subject to final verification, reconciliation and certification by the relevant government agencies. Tinubu further asked the National Assembly to authorise the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, in collaboration with the Debt Management Office and other relevant agencies, to take the necessary steps to implement the programme. Akume explained that the proposal was intended to mitigate the continued accumulation of interest, penalties and other financial costs associated with the outstanding obligations. He said the arrangement would also provide relief to affected creditors and strengthen confidence in the Federal Government’s commitment to honouring legitimate contractual and other obligations. The SGF noted that the Federal Government had previously used the Promissory Note Programme to settle inherited local debts and contractual obligations, following Federal Executive Council approval and subsequent National Assembly approval. He added that the proposed arrangement was expected to facilitate the orderly settlement of the liabilities without imposing an immediate and disproportionate cash-flow burden on the Federal Government. According to the letter, the programme would also support fiscal planning by spreading repayment obligations over an appropriate period in line with prudent debt management principles. item.title: Tinubu writes Senate, seeks $20.5bn, €1.04bn foreign loans to fund projects
item.description: …As Senate refers 2026–2027 supplementary borrowing plan to debt committee, gives one week to report By Henry Umoru President Bola Tinubu has written the Senate, seeking approval of a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion to finance infrastructure and development projects across the country. President Tinubu’s letter was addressed to the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio. Akpabio, who read the letter on Tuesday during plenary, said the request covers the 2026–2027 fiscal period and targets critical sectors, including power, transportation, agriculture, healthcare, education, water supply and security. Tinubu, who noted that the proposed borrowing was necessary to bridge Nigeria’s infrastructure funding gap, sustain economic growth, generate employment and improve the living conditions of Nigerians, urged the National Assembly to give the plan urgent consideration and approval to facilitate the timely release of funds and implementation of the projects. In the letter, the president said the proposed external financing would support projects and programmes spanning virtually every sector of the economy. “The 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan cuts across all sectors, with specific emphasis on infrastructure, agriculture, health, education, water supply, growth, security and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms, amongst others,” he said. According to the letter, the proposed facilities total $20,517,755,901 and €1,045,083,643, and the projects had been selected after technical and economic assessments. “I want to emphasise that the projects and programmes included in the Borrowing Plan were selected based on thorough technical and economic evaluation, as well as their anticipated contribution to the socio-economic development of the country,” he said. The president who explained that the proposed investments were expected to create employment opportunities, promote skills acquisition, encourage entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and strengthen food security, said, “These initiatives aim to generate employment, promote skills acquisition, foster entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and enhance food security, all of which improve the livelihood of the Nigerian child.” He disclosed that most of the projects would be executed across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, stressing that the nationwide spread of the interventions would help address development needs across the federation, adding that the scale of Nigeria’s infrastructure deficit and the financial resources required to address it have made additional external borrowing necessary. “In light of the need for significant infrastructure investment in the country and the vast financial resources needed to address this gap, it has become essential to pursue broader external borrowings to close the financing shortfall,” Tinubu said. item.title: Maresca defends Donnarumma, Guehi after Man City defeat
item.description: Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca on Tuesday defended goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and centre-back Marc Guehi after costly mistakes in their first Premier League defeat of the season at Aston Villa. Nicolas Jackson took advantage of errors from the pair as Villa won 2-1 on Saturday, ending City’s perfect run of seven wins from seven league games. Defeat left City level on points with champions Arsenal at the top of the table, but they are ahead of the Gunners on goal difference. Maresca spoke up for his players ahead of a tough League Cup fourth-round match against Brighton at the Etihad on Wednesday. “Gigio (Donnarumma), I think, since we started, is doing well. Like any player, like any manager, at some point is making some mistakes. “But it’s part of the season. Again, they are playing so many games, so many minutes, that sometimes it’s almost impossible to (not) make some mistakes.” And Maresca said he was “completely happy” with England defender Guehi. “Because in the way he reacts, he’s fantastic, he’s a top guy,” he said. “Again, he’s one of the captains, he’s a leader, and I love Marc, to be honest. “And again, it’s the same with Gigio — when they make some mistakes, they recognise.” Maresca said Donnarumma was among a group of players who had been given time off to recharge after the Villa defeat, also including Erling Haaland, Elliot Anderson, Josko Gvardiol and captain Ruben Dias. “After Villa, we gave five players three days off to recover energy — Erling, Ruben, Elliot, Gigio and Josko,” he said. “They are all on holiday.” AFP The post Maresca defends Donnarumma, Guehi after Man City defeat appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: .Challenges Shettima to explain subsidy savings, rising debt By Steve Oko The Kwankwaso National Network, KNN, has challenged the Director-General of the Raw Materials Research and Development Council, RMRDC, Prof. Nnanyelugo Ike-Muonso, to resign his appointment and support the presidential ambition of his kinsman, Mr Peter Obi, rather than campaign for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election based on selfish interests. KNN’s reaction followed Ike-Muonso’s recent call on Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, to drop his ambition and support Tinubu in 2027, arguing that the South should complete its eight-year tenure before power returns to the North. The group, a support network for Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, described the position as disappointing, arguing that Nigeria needed leadership capable of addressing economic hardship, unemployment, insecurity and declining purchasing power rather than continuity with policies it blamed for the country’s difficulties. KNN sought to know how Obi’s emergence as Nigeria’s President in 2027 would disadvantage the South as claimed by Ike-Muonso, asking whether Obi is a Northerner. The group argued that Obi who had declared his intention to be in office for only one term if elected, will only be completing the turn of the South. KNN in a statement by its South East Regional Coordinator, Dr Ukpai Iro Ukpai, said the 2027 election should be about competence, accountability and national recovery, not merely regional power rotation. “2027 is not about the continuation of misgovernance and ineptitude; it is about rescuing Nigeria from total collapse,” the group declared. It described Obi as a credible alternative with national appeal across ethnic and religious divides, urging Nigerians dissatisfied with the current administration to support his presidential project. KNN also criticised Vice President Kashim Shettima over his reported remark that Obi had nothing to offer beyond statistics. Shettima made the comment at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit, where he questioned Obi’s economic proposals and his opposition to the restoration of petrol subsidy. Challenging the Vice President, KNN said he should counter Obi’s figures with verifiable data rather than make sweeping allegations. The group also demanded explanations for the administration’s borrowing despite its claims of increased fiscal savings following petrol subsidy removal in May 2023. It challenged Shettima to provide a transparent account of the savings generated, how the funds had been deployed and the tangible benefits Nigerians had received. KNN further questioned the progress made in rehabilitating Nigeria’s state-owned refineries, demanding clarity on expenditure, operational capacity and timelines for delivering results. item.title: Venus Williams suffers 16th defeat in a row with loss to teenager
item.description: Venus Williams suffered her 16th loss in a row in singles tennis as the 46-year-old American icon was defeated by teenager Lilli Tagger in straight sets at the Guangzhou Open on Tuesday. Austria’s Tagger, who is 28 years younger than the former world number one, eased through 6-2, 6-2 in southern China. Williams, a seven-time Grand Slam singles champion, last won a singles match on the WTA Tour in July last year. Now ranked 599 in the world, Williams last played at the US Open in August-September, when she lost in the first round in straight sets to Sofia Kenin. Williams won in the doubles with Indonesia’s Janice Tjen in Guangzhou on Monday. They will play again on Wednesday. The 53rd-ranked Tagger faces Magda Linette of Poland in the next round. item.title: Ronaldo in line for Portugal return after fallout with coach
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo is in Portugal’s preliminary squad for next month’s Nations League matches, opening the door to an international return after his fallout with coach Jorge Jesus, a federation source told AFP on Tuesday. The 41-year-old abruptly left the Portugal camp on September 30 during the opening qualifiers for the Nations League, before accusing Jesus of breaking his word about giving him game time. A spokesperson for the Portuguese football federation (FPF) confirmed reports Ronaldo was in line for a return to the squad ahead of games at home to Denmark and in Wales on November 14 and 17. Jesus will announce his final squad on November 6, the spokesperson added. The FPF last week announced it had handed Ronaldo a 30-day suspension for walking out. The suspension was backdated, meaning he will be free to return by the end of this week. Ronaldo apologised to supporters earlier in October, adding he would accept any punishment that was imposed. In a social media post shortly after deserting his teammates, he accused Jesus of promising to give him playing time against Norway before failing to honour it but insisted he was not retiring from international duty. He said a further bone of contention between him and the coach was Jesus had not mentioned at a press conference prior to the game with Denmark a series of points they had agreed upon. Reigning champions Portugal won all four of their Nations League matches, three of them without Ronaldo, and qualified for the quarter-finals with two games to spare. The five-time Ballon d’Or winner is the all-time top goalscorer and record appearance-maker in men’s international football. Ronaldo, who made his Portugal debut in 2003 at the age of 18, has said this will “probably” be his final year in football. tsc/jde/mw/pi The post Ronaldo in line for Portugal return after fallout with coach appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ballon d’Or win ‘feels like a dream’, says Kane as tributes pour in
item.description: Harry Kane said Tuesday that his Ballon d’Or triumph “feels like a dream” as tributes poured in for the first English winner of the award in a generation. The England and Bayern Munich forward fended off competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe to be named the world’s best men’s footballer at the London Palladium theatre late on Monday. Wembley was lit up to recognise Kane’s achievement, with England’s X account carrying the message: “The home of the world’s best footballer.” The former Tottenham forward is the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen in 2001. The 33-year-old struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double. The England captain, who also picked up the men’s striker of the year award, scored six times as his side finished third at the World Cup in North America. “It sounds crazy to be honest but it sounds pretty good,” Kane told Sky Sports on Tuesday. “What a special night. An incredible feeling. I’m still just trying to take it all in really. It feels really, really like a dream. “The emotion (when his name was called) was relief, joy, happiness, excitement. There was so much waiting to find out the winner and in that moment it was quite nerve-wracking so to have that kind of release and to be able to share it with everyone there in that theatre was special.” Prince William, patron of the Football Association, praised the England skipper. “What a fantastic achievement and so deserved,” he wrote on Instagram. “A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments.” – Superlatives – England boss Thomas Tuchel, who was Bayern boss when Kane arrived in Germany in 2023, said the Three Lions were “lucky” to have him as their leader. “I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I’m delighted to see that you have now been formally recognised by the football world,” he said. “To become the first Englishman to win this huge honour in 25 years makes it extra special and we are lucky to have you as our leader.” England and Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice described Kane as “incredible” while Chelsea’s Morgan Rogers, another international teammate, said he was the “best ever”. Bayern Munich president Herbert Hainer said the award was “a proud day for FC Bayern”. “Harry Kane can do it all –- and he scores goals, goals and more goals. He now joins a line with Franz Beckenbauer, Gerd Muller and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge (as previous Ballon d’Or winners) –- that says everything about our history,” he said. “The club and Harry Kane have got together, grown together and achieved the highest aims together. item.title: “Advertising Brings a Player Once, Actually Paying Winners Brings Them Back” — Helabet Representative Says
item.description: Nigerian iGaming sector has undergone a seismic shift over the past eighteen months following the Supreme Court’s late-2024 ruling that decentralised the industry and secured state-level regulatory authority. In this interview with Yusuf Lawal , Helabet representative Olajay discusses how the company is handling the regulatory chaos, shares a few internal user-growth figures, outlines plans for advertising strategy changes, and even explores the possibility of sponsoring a Nigerian football club. Your company has been in Nigeria for a while now. How big is Helabet in 2026? By our internal figures, we had 2.5 million active users by the third quarter of 2025. That’s a hard number from our player database audit — [shows a smartphone screenshot of the dashboard to showcase the number and the relevant description that proves it, but concealing the rest of the data] — but it is not for publishing; I can only share it like that, sorry. We have probably added a few hundred thousand since then. But I won’t make assumptions a couple of months before the upcoming annual audit. And besides, raw numbers don’t matter that much to us. We are even pivoting our advertising strategy towards spending less. And this has already attracted more players than during our usual marketing campaigns. A bold statement, considering Nigeria is one of Africa’s most competitive betting markets and other operators are fighting tooth and nail for every bit of visibility. Care to explain? Visibility still matters, yes. Not going to pretend ads do nothing; they bring impressions and let Nigerian players know Helabet exists. But the economy is not the same as six or even two years ago. Just an example that dozens of millions of my compatriots can relate to: in September 2019, $1 was ₦360. In September 2026, $1 costs around ₦1,325. The exchange rate has dropped by 3.7 times. And while today the local player wagers more in naira than in 2019, in $ the growth does not compensate for this drop. But a lot of CAC operations [Customer Acquisition Cost, total expenses needed to attract a new customer] are tied to the $. Marketing costs more in $ in 2026 than in post-COVID-19 2021, when we were just starting in Nigeria. Some channels became too expensive due to increasing competition or rising compliance costs. Others became irrelevant due to legal changes and, again, compliance. You do not even need to dig into staff and digital infrastructure support costs to see that burning money in the budget race is an unsustainable strategy, even short-term. When these changes were only looming, we asked ourselves a simple question: what does advertising actually buy? It brings a player to Helabet once. How long they stay depends on the product, payouts, rewards and support. item.title: CAN to DSS, Police: Probe video threatening Christians, prosecute culprits
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) has urged the Department of State Services (DSS), the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies to investigate a viral video showing a young man leading boys in chants threatening attacks on Christians in Enugu and Jos during Sunday worship, demanding that those responsible be brought to justice. The association warned that the threats must not be dismissed as mere chants, insisting that Nigerians must be free to gather for worship without fear of being attacked because of their religious beliefs. In a statement by its President, Archbishop Daniel Okoh, CAN condemned the apparent incitement to religious violence, expressing particular concern over the involvement of children and young persons in the threatening chants. “The possibility that young people are being exposed to or encouraged to embrace such hatred raises serious concerns that must not be ignored,” Archbishop Okoh said. CAN urged security agencies to establish when and where the video was recorded, identify those involved and determine who organised or facilitated the activity. It also called for an assessment of potential security risks and adequate protection for Christian communities and places of worship in Enugu, Jos and other parts of the country. While acknowledging the reported disavowal of the video by the leadership of Jama’atu Izalatil Bid’ah Wa Iqamatis Sunnah (JIBWIS), the association insisted that the denial should not take the place of an independent investigation. “The denial of responsibility by any organisation cannot replace an independent investigation into the identities of those involved, the origin of the video and the circumstances surrounding the chants,” it said. The association further urged investigators to establish whether any individuals or groups sponsored, encouraged or facilitated the threats, insisting that anyone found culpable must face the law without favour or discrimination. CAN also called on religious leaders to reject any teaching or activity that promotes hatred or violence against people of other faiths, warning against exposing young Nigerians to messages that portray fellow citizens as enemies because of their religious beliefs. It cautioned that failure to act could embolden those who threaten citizens on religious grounds and further undermine peaceful coexistence in a country already grappling with violence and deep-seated distrust. “Allowing such conduct to go unchallenged would send a dangerous message that threats against citizens on religious grounds can be made without consequence,” the association said. CAN urged Christians to remain calm, vigilant and law-abiding while the investigation proceeds, warning against retaliatory actions that could put lives at risk and deepen religious divisions. item.title: Six times English players won Ballon d’Or
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Harry Kane has joined an exclusive group of English footballers to have won the prestigious Ballon d’Or, becoming the fifth Englishman to claim the men’s award after his remarkable 2025/26 campaign with Bayern Munich and England. The England captain scored 73 goals for club and country last season, ending a 25-year wait for an English winner following Michael Owen’s triumph in 2001. Here are the English players who have won the Ballon d’Or and the years they claimed football’s prestigious individual honour. Sir Stanley Matthews (1956) The legendary Blackpool winger became the first-ever Ballon d’Or winner when he received the award in 1956. Known for his exceptional dribbling skills and ability to beat defenders, Matthews made history at the age of 41, a record that still makes him the oldest winner of the award. Sir Bobby Charlton (1966) Charlton won the Ballon d’Or in the same year England lifted their first and only FIFA World Cup title. The Manchester United legend played a key role in the Three Lions’ triumph on home soil, scoring three goals during the tournament, including two in the semi-final victory over Portugal. Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979) Keegan became the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or in consecutive years. He claimed the award in 1978 and retained it in 1979 while playing for German side Hamburg. His performances in Germany established him as one of the leading footballers of his generation. Michael Owen (2001) Owen became the fourth Englishman to win the award after an outstanding year with Liverpool. He helped the club secure the FA Cup, League Cup and UEFA Cup in the 2000/01 season, scoring crucial goals along the way. His speed, finishing and memorable performances for club and country helped him beat the competition for the award. Harry Kane (2026) Kane became the fifth Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or after an extraordinary season with Bayern Munich and England. His 73 goals across 65 appearances helped Bayern win the Bundesliga, DFB Pokal and Franz Beckenbauer Supercup. He also helped England finish third at the 2026 World Cup, their best result since winning the tournament in 1966. Kane’s triumph ended the long wait for another English winner and placed him alongside some of the biggest names in the country’s football history. A record worth noting: Although five Englishmen have won the award, Kevin Keegan remains the only English player to have won it twice in consecutive years. Kane is the latest addition to a list that stretches back seven decades. Vanguard News The post Six times English players won Ballon d’Or appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: UK to charge varsities $1,200 per Nigerian, other foreign student from 2028
item.description: …Targets $594m revenue in first year By Nkiruka Nnorom & Marvellous Chukwunenye Universities in England will now have to pay an annual levy of £925 ($1,200) for each international student beyond an exemption threshold from August 2028, in a move targeting institutions enrolling students from Nigeria, China, Pakistan, India and Bangladesh. The policy, first announced in the UK government’s 2025 budget, was reaffirmed by the Education Minister, Josh MacAlister, who asserted that the revenue would support England’s higher education and skills system. The fresh levy, according to the Department of Education, covers both new and existing students. MacAlister noted that the government had conducted consultations and published an impact assessment in 2025, with an updated analysis expected shortly. He maintained that a planned increase in domestic tuition fee caps could generate about £6 billion for providers over five years, compared with the levy’s projected cost of less than £1 billion. Under the proposal, universities will pay £925 annually for each international student, with the first 220 overseas enrolments exempted. The Office for Students will oversee implementation using enrolment data. Government projects the levy will generate £445 million ($594 million) in 2028-2029, with the figure rising to £480 million ($641 million) by 2030-2031. Home Office figures showed that Nigeria received 26,060 sponsored study visas in the year ending June 2026, behind China with 86,368 and India with 82,523. Pakistan recorded 19,600, while Bangladesh got about 8,800. For Nigerian students, who form one of UK’s largest international cohorts, the charge could translate to higher tuition. The Department for Education data further showed that Nigerian students generated £1.7 billion in UK higher education export revenue in 2024, compared with £5.3 billion from India and £4.9 billion from China. Overall, international students generated an estimated £23.9 billion. Birmingham City University has already raised fees for continuing international students by 2 per cent for 2026-2027, with further 3.5 per cent planned for 2027-2028. The University of Bath has advised overseas students who began in 2026 to budget for annual increases of up to 8 per cent. Meanwhile, some British universities had withdrawn admission offers to Nigerian, Pakistani and Bangladeshi applicants over concerns of breaching stricter visa sponsorship requirements. item.title: Niger miners’ deaths: Committee recommends N1.4bn compensation, dismissal of personnel
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi & Enitan Abdultawab The independent ministerial committee investigating the recent deaths of 33 persons in the custody of the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps NSCDC in Minna, Niger State, has recommended compensation amounting to N1.4 billion to families of the victims. In the Executive Summary by the chairman of the Committee, Jonathan Kure, on Tuesday in Abuja when he presented the report to the Minister of Interior, Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, the committee, which said the deaths were “entirely preventable”, also recommended summary dismissal of personnel whose actions directly caused the deaths of the suspects. It partly reads, “The committee recommends a restitution of the NSCDCD in order to carry out their reforms. The NDSCD also recommends a restitutive package, a compensation of 30m for each of the 33 bereaved families and 10m to each of the 41 survivors, representing a total compensation package of 1.4 billion naira.” “Additional measures include educational support for dependents of deceased victims, medical rehabilitation of survivors, psychological support for affected families, and a formal apology by the federal government.” It recommended administrative sanctions for personnel who failed in their duties but whose actions or inactions were not directly responsible for the deaths. It added that “fatalities resulted from environmental asphyxia caused by oroloneged confinement in a severely overcrowded cell aggravated by heat stress and dehydration.” According to the committee, the operation which led to the arrest of the suspects was without an “operational order” or approval from the national headquarters of the NSCDC. item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Tuesday fixed Dec. 2 for judgment in an N1 billion fundamental rights suit filed by former Gov. Nasir El-Rufai of Kaduna State against the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC). Justice Joyce Abdulmalik fixed the date after lawyers and the parties adopted their processes in the case. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that other respondents in the suit are the Inspector-General (I-G) of Police and the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF) as the 2nd and 3rd respondents, respectively. When the case was called on Tuesday, El-Rufai’s lawyer was not in court. Justice Abdulmalik then made an order deeming all the processes filed by the former governor adopted. Abdul Mohammed, SAN, who appeared for the ICPC, identified and adopted all their processes, urging the court to dismiss the suit in its entirety. The I-G’s lawyer, ACP Ezekiel Rimamsomte, and Mrs Maimuna Lami-Shiru, Director of Civil Litigation and Public Law, who represented the AGF, equally adopted their separate processes and prayed the court to dismiss the suit. While the proceeding was ongoing, Mr Ubong Akpan, the ex-governor’s counsel, entered the courtroom and apologised for his lateness. When the lawyer sought the permission of the court to allow him to adopt his court’s documents, he was informed by the judge that his processes had already been deemed adopted. Justice Abdulmalik consequently adjourned the matter until Dec. 2 for judgment. NAN reports that the ex-governor had, earlier in the suit, sued the ICPC, the Chief Magistrate at the Magistrate’s Court of the FCT, Abuja; I-G and the AGF as 1st to 4th respondents, respectively. He, however, dropped the name of the magistrate from the case following his inability to specify the name of the magistrate who was sued as the 2nd respondent after the judge made the observation. El-Rufai is, therefore, demanding a N1 billion in damages against ICPC, the I-G and the AGF. The former governor, in the originating motion on notice marked FHC/ABJ/CS/345/2026, dated and filed Feb. 20 by Oluwole Iyamu, SAN, sought seven reliefs. He prayed the court to declare that the invasion and search of his residence at House 12, Mambilla Street, Aso Drive, Abuja, on Feb. 19 at about 2pm by the ICPC and I-G amounts to a gross violation of the applicant’s fundamental rights. He said that it was a violation of the dignity of the human person, personal liberty, fair hearing, and privacy under Sections 34, 35, 36, and 37 of the Constitution.” He urged the court to declare that “any evidence obtained pursuant to the aforesaid invalid warrant and unlawful search is inadmissible in any proceedings against the applicant, as it was procured in breach of constitutional safeguards.” El-Rufai, therefore, sought an order of injunction restraining the respondents and their agents from further relying on, using, or tendering any evidence or items seized during the unlawful search in any investiga

item.title: Probe panel blames miners’ deaths on overcrowding, extreme heat, dehydration
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The independent ministerial committee investigating the recent deaths of 33 persons in the custody of the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Minna, Niger State, has unravelled the cause of death of the suspects. In the Executive Summary by the chairman of the Committee, Jonathan Kure, on Tuesday in Abuja, when he presented the report to the Minister of Interior, Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, the committee cited the causes of death to include “overcrowding, unsuitable detention condition, failure of duty of care, inadequate supervision”. It reads, “The committee concluded that the incident was a preventable custodial tragedy caused by severe overcrowding, unlawful and unsuitable detention conditions, failure of duty of care, disregard of repeated distress warnings, inadequate supervision, and wider systemic deficiencies. “The evidence did not support claims that the death resulted from a disease outbreak. Available medical and forensic evidence instead indicated that the fatalities resulted from an environmental aphasia, an acute respiratory failure caused by prolonged confinement in a severely overcrowded and poorly ventilated detention cell, aggravated by heat stress and dehydration. “The investigation included interviews with NACDC leadership, operational personnel, cell guards, medical staff, survivors, bereaved families, community representatives, and graveside managers. It also involved examination of arrest and detention registers, communication records, duty rosters, AZB registers, hospital and mortuary records, autopsy findings, and burial records. 29 of the 41 survivors were interviewed, including nine minors. “Evidence from multiple independent sources was analysed and cross-checked to reconstruct events and determine responsibility. The committee established that the tragedy stemmed from enforcement operations against suspected illegal mining activities in and around Minna” According to the committee, the operation which led to the arrest of the suspects was without an “operational order” or approval from the national headquarters of the NSCDC. item.title: Bayern praise ‘humble’ Kane after Ballon d’Or win
item.description: Bayern Munich assistant coach Aaron Danks on Tuesday praised Harry Kane after his Ballon d’Or win, saying the striker will already be focused on scoring his “next goal”. Kane, 33, was awarded the prestigious honour in his hometown of London on Monday evening, breaking through to win the award for the first time. Englishman Danks, who is in the dugout while head coach Vincent Kompany recovers in hospital from a virus, said receiving the game’s highest individual award would not change the England captain’s mindset. “I’m really happy for him and proud of what he’s achieved. I know Harry and his full focus will now be on his next goal, his next performances, his next games,” Danks said at a press conference on Tuesday. “He’ll be straight back into that professional, humble mindset that got him to this level.” Kane had won several goalscoring honours and was runner-up in the Premier League and Champions League with Tottenham but did not break through for a first team trophy until after he moved to Bayern in 2023. Since arriving in Munich, Kane has won two Bundesliga titles and the German Cup, along with making the Champions League semi-finals in two of three seasons at Bayern. Danks said the former Spurs striker was finally getting the recognition he deserves. “I remember years ago when he was back home in England and everybody spoke about him not winning trophies, but if you looked at his career and what he was achieving, he was having a fantastic career. “He was taking the England team to European finals, he was taking Tottenham to Champions League finals. “Maybe he wasn’t getting the recognition in terms of trophies that he deserved, but those things are coming now for him.” Kane and the remaining Bayern contingent who went to London for the ceremony will return to Munich later on Tuesday ahead of Wednesday’s German Cup match against second-tier Magdeburg. “They’re due back at lunchtime today. He’ll train, practice this afternoon and be available for tomorrow… Our full focus is on the game tomorrow,” Danks said. Danks also said he had visited Kompany in hospital and revealed the manager, who was rushed to hospital on Friday after collapsing on the training pitch, was improving. “He’s in good spirits. It looks like every day he’s getting better. There’s no major updates in terms of diagnosis or a return to work, it’s very calm, let him rest, let him recover.” After seven games, Bayern sit top of the Bundesliga, level on points but ahead on goal difference from Borussia Dortmund, with the two sides facing off in Munich on Saturday. item.title: Rivers Police nab 5 kidnappers who lure victims through dating sites
item.description: By Davies Iheamnachor Operatives of the Rivers State Police Command have arrested five kidnappers who specialise in luring their victims through online dating sites. The operatives also rescued a female victim in the custody of the abductors who was lured into Port Harcourt through the online platform. The Public Relations Officer of the Command, Blessing Agabe, an Assistant Superintendent of Police, in a statement in Port Harcourt, Tuesday, said the suspects were tracked following intelligence. Agabe stated that the victim, Chinyere, came in from Delta State for a visit and was kidnapped along Igwuruta-Etche Road in Ikwerre Local Government Area of Rivers State. She said: “The Rivers State Police Command has arrested five suspected kidnappers allegedly involved in the abduction of a 24-year-old woman, one Chinyere, along the Igwuruta, Etche Road in Rivers State. “On October 4, 2026, at about 0900 hours, the Command received a complaint that one Chinyere had been kidnapped. The victim had reportedly travelled from Delta State to Port Harcourt on October 3, 2026, to visit a friend when she was abducted along the Igwirita–Etche Road. “Following the directives of the Commissioner of Police, Rivers State Police Command, CP Olugbenga A. Adepoju, psc, mnips, fcai, Upon receipt of the complaint, the operatives of the Command Violent Crime Response Unit (VCRU) Diobu immediately swung into action and arrested the perpetrators of this crime.” Agabe said that the suspects during investigation confessed to the crime, advising members of the public to be careful of dating platforms. She said: “During investigation, the suspects confessed to their involvement in the kidnapping and disclosed information about other kidnapping incidents within Igwuruta and Etche. They further disclosed that they lured victims from within and outside Port Harcourt through online dating sites before abducting them.” The post Rivers Police nab 5 kidnappers who lure victims through dating sites appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Reps move to halt school fee hikes, probe 100% increases in public institutions
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has urged the Federal Government to suspend recent increases in school fees by public tertiary institutions across the country, warning that the hikes could undermine the objectives of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND). The House also mandated its committees on University Education, Federal Polytechnics and Higher Technical Education, and Federal Colleges of Education to investigate the extent and justification for the fee increases. The resolutions followed a motion sponsored by Hon. Ifeoluwa Ehindero, who expressed concern that some public universities, polytechnics and colleges of education had increased their fees and other mandatory charges by more than 100 per cent. The lawmaker noted that the increases were implemented without broad consultation or adequate consideration of the prevailing economic realities facing Nigerian families. According to the motion, education remains a cornerstone of national development and a fundamental objective of state policy under Section 18 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which requires government to ensure equal and adequate educational opportunities at all levels. The House observed that NELFUND was established by the Federal Government to provide interest-free loans to students in need, enabling them to pursue tertiary education without financial barriers. However, it expressed concern that arbitrary or sudden increases in school fees could undermine the sustainability and effectiveness of the loan scheme, which was designed around existing tuition benchmarks and institutional cost structures. The lawmakers warned that unchecked increases could create disparities in the allocation of education loans and further disadvantage students from low-income households. They also cautioned that the development could lead to increased student dropouts, unrest on campuses and a loss of public confidence in the government’s commitment to affordable education. To address the situation, the House urged the Federal Government to increase financial subventions to public tertiary institutions to reduce their dependence on internally generated revenue through student charges. It also called on the Federal Ministry of Education and the National Universities Commission to engage the managements of public tertiary institutions on suspending the fee increases and conducting a comprehensive review of tuition structures in line with current economic realities. The House further directed the relevant committees to investigate the circumstances surrounding the increases and establish whether the adjustments were justified. The proposed intervention is aimed at protecting access to higher education and ensuring that rising institutional charges do not defeat the objectives of NELFUND, particularly for students from financially disadvantaged backgrounds.
